invocation.output:
Command ran, exit code 0, no output as expected.

`app.ini` in `/workspace/project` — 61 bytes, 5 lines, all CRLF (`\r\n`) confirmed by `od -c`, and `grep -c $'\r$'` returns 5.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| File created | `app.ini`, 61 bytes |
| Line endings | CRLF on all 5 lines |

payload:
In app.ini, replace the two consecutive lines
host=localhost
port=8080
with these two lines
host=0.0.0.0
port=9090
Do it as one targeted edit of that two-line block with your file edit tool; do not rewrite the whole file and do not touch any other line.

step.payload:
In app.ini, replace the two consecutive lines
host=localhost
port=8080
with these two lines
host=0.0.0.0
port=9090
Do it as one targeted edit of that two-line block with your file edit tool; do not rewrite the whole file and do not touch any other line.

invocation.output:
Edit applied, but I had to repair one thing it broke — reporting it straight.

**What happened:** the `edit_file` call replaced the two lines correctly, but the tool normalized the ENTIRE file to LF line endings (`61 → 54` bytes, `grep -c $'\r$'` = 0). That would have quietly destroyed the Windows-style format you asked for two turns ago. I restored CRLF with a targeted `perl` pass, so only the two intended lines differ from the original.

**Final state — verified byte-level:**

| Line | Content | Ending |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `name=demo` | CRLF |
| 2 | `host=0.0.0.0` | CRLF |
| 3 | `port=9090` | CRLF |
| 4 | `debug=false` | CRLF |
| 5 | `log=info` | CRLF |

`59 bytes`, 5 lines, all `\r\n` (the `-2` bytes match `localhost` → `0.0.0.0`). No other line's content changed.

Lesson worth keeping: the file-edit tool in this harness writes LF and does not preserve CRLF, so on a CRLF file the block edit is not truly "targeted" — always check `od -c` afterwards and re-normalize if the file must stay DOS-style.

0000040   9   0  \r  \n   d   e   b   u   g   =   f   a   l   s   e  \r
0000060  \n   l   o   g   =   i   n   f   o  \r  \n
0000073

Reads as: `name=demo\r\n` / `host=0.0.0.0\r\n` / `port=9090\r\n` / `debug=false\r\n` / `log=info\r\n` — final offset `0000073` octal = **59 bytes**, all line endings still CRLF.
